1. Betrek je kinderen bij de voorbereidi: 1. Involve your children in the preparations
Kinderen voelen zich veiliger als ze beg: Children feel safer when they understand what's happening. Tell them in good time that you're moving house and explain why. Show them the new house, or look at photos of the neighbourhood together. Young children enjoy 'choosing' a room or helping to pack their own toy boxes. This makes them feel involved and important.
Plan de verhuizing in een vakantie. Dit: Plan the removal during a holiday. This is the most pleasant option for the child, as they have some time off and there's nothing else stressful going on, such as an important test. If your child is changing schools, it's easiest for them to move in the summer, so they can get used to the new house first and then start at the new school afterwards.

3. Richt de nieuwe kamer samen in: 3. Set up the new room together
Niets is zo belangrijk voor kinderen als: Nothing is as important to children as their own space. Let them help set up their new room, whether it's the colour of the walls or choosing a new poster. This way, the new house starts to feel familiar more quickly.
Het is normaal dat kinderen even moeten: It's normal for children to need some time to get used to the new situation. Give them time, listen to their feelings and make room for questions. Before long, they'll feel completely at home again.
